target_strategy.positioning: Position Denys Strakhov as a backend-focused TypeScript engineer for resilient APIs, integrations and asynchronous data workflows, with commercial Node.js/Azure production experience and a strong PostgreSQL foundation.
target_strategy.main_angle: The primary angle is resilient, integration-heavy backend engineering for APIs and data workflows. The three strongest supporting arguments are: 1) ProductsUp product synchronization, backed by the ProductsUp career case, demonstrates long-running asynchronous workflows, Durable Functions, retries, idempotency, Blob Storage, streaming and processing of approximately 20,000–40,000 products per sync; 2) Amplience automation and CommerceTools integration, backed by the Amplience and CommerceTools career cases, demonstrate external API integration, data transformation, webhook-driven workflows, product-data modeling and e-commerce-scale processing; 3) the EPAM platform overview and customer notification incident, backed by the EPAM and customer notification career cases, demonstrate commercial Node.js/TypeScript delivery, production debugging, observability, event-driven service collaboration and business-critical reliability work.
risk_mitigation: Describe asynchronous messaging as Azure queue/topic/subscription triggers and confirmed Azure Service Bus subscription experience; do not claim deep ownership of a generic queue platform.
Use Cosmos DB as commercial document-database experience and a transferable MongoDB signal, but do not claim deep MongoDB expertise or NoSQL architecture ownership.
Keep Express and MongoDB limited to the CHI internship/training context and exclude them from top skills.
Present JobFlow and AI Job Assistant as personal portfolio evidence, not commercial AI production or enterprise agent-platform experience.
Frame EPAM ownership as implementation and key contribution within team-owned services, not sole architecture ownership.
Do not claim creative-performance, advertising analytics or Motion-domain experience; emphasize transferable e-commerce data and integration experience.
Keep React/Next.js as backend-focused fullstack contribution rather than frontend specialization.
Use PostgreSQL as a strong commercial foundation from Factor–IT, while avoiding claims that it was the primary recent EPAM datastore.

cv_content.headline: Backend-focused TypeScript Engineer | Node.js | Azure | APIs | Async Data Workflows
summary: Backend-focused TypeScript engineer based in Cologne, Germany, with commercial production experience building Node.js services, Azure Functions and third-party API integrations.
Delivered resilient e-commerce workflows using Durable Functions, asynchronous triggers, retries, idempotency, Cosmos DB, Blob Storage and streaming data processing.
Strong PostgreSQL foundation from production financial systems, including complex SQL, migrations, transactions and data-integrity work.
Experienced with production debugging, Application Insights/KQL, Jest testing and backend-focused React/Next.js delivery.
Authorized to work in Germany; additional personal portfolio work explores AI-assisted backend workflows and OpenAI API integration.

current_work_block.role_line: Freelance Software Development, Backend Portfolio Projects & Relocation
current_work_block.stable_intro: Continued active software development after relocating from Ukraine to Germany through small freelance tasks, backend-focused portfolio projects, structured upskilling, and local volunteering.

bullets.text: Supported small Node.js/React improvements on an independent basis, including feature additions, bug fixes, API-related changes, UI adjustments and maintenance tasks.

Built JobFlow CV Pipeline, a backend-first NestJS/TypeScript portfolio project for vacancy analysis, targeted CV generation, evidence-based claim validation and deterministic PDF export; implemented human-in-the-loop AI workflow concepts, Evidence Guard, prompt versioning, artifact traceability, token/cost tracking and backend HTML-to-PDF export without AI token usage.
Continued Python/FastAPI backend learning through personal projects using PostgreSQL, SQLAlchemy, Pytest, OpenAI API and GitHub Actions.
Volunteer IT Technician at HEY, ALTER! Köln e.V., refurbishing donated laptops for school students in Cologne.
Worked on a large-scale multi-locale e-commerce platform for a major European retailer, delivering Node.js/TypeScript backend services in an Azure serverless environment supporting 18+ locales.

Built the initial implementation and later maintained/contributed to a ProductsUp product synchronization flow using Azure Durable Functions, CommerceTools enrichment, Azure Blob Storage and Stream API uploads.

Supported long-running product synchronization processing approximately 20,000–40,000 products per sync across changed locales, using activity-level retries, idempotency handling, failed-product logging and per-locale result summaries.
bullets.evidence_source: Career_Case_Deep_Dives_RU_v0_6_current_work_sync.md — Case 1, ProductsUp scale and reliability evidence

bullets.text: Automated selected Amplience CMS workflows with webhook-based Azure Functions, handling create/update/publish/unpublish events, validation, logging, retries, cache updates and mass field-update logic; reduced selected manual operations from hours to minutes.

Integrated CommerceTools product data into PDP, listing, BFF/backend and ProductsUp enrichment flows, handling up to approximately 100,000 unique products, 50+ attributes, optional fields, pagination where supported and custom batching where needed.

Investigated production issues using Azure Application Insights and KQL, tracing failures across Azure Functions, BFF layers and backend services and contributing to improved logging and alerting for business-critical notification flows.
Worked on an event-driven customer notification flow, processing subscription-based events, enriching missing data and formatting payloads for downstream email/SMS services.

Wrote and maintained function-level backend unit tests with Jest, mocked external dependencies and worked within SonarQube quality gates while collaborating with QA, BA, Product Owners, DevOps and other service teams.

Developed backend functionality for a production public-sector budget accounting system, focusing on PostgreSQL-heavy features, complex business logic, financial data integrity and legacy backend maintenance.

Implemented high-risk PostgreSQL migrations for financial accounting data, including multi-table account-splitting changes with transactions, validation on test databases and rollback planning where possible.
Wrote complex SQL using joins, subqueries and indexes and contributed to query optimization and data-integrity improvements in a PostgreSQL-backed financial system.
Contributed to a custom in-house PHP backend framework, improving database access, migrations, validation, permissions and backend routing.

Completed a full-time Node.js transition internship focused on moving from PHP to JavaScript backend development, covering REST APIs, introductory Express and NestJS, MongoDB, Docker basics and code review.
